items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
items.summary: The article explores using sensorimotor alignment as a low-cost offline proxy to gauge robotic foundation model performance, linking vision, language, and motion representations.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a cheaper, scalable way to evaluate and improve multi-modal robotics systems.

items.title: Direct Pass@k Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
items.summary: The paper proposes a Direct Pass@k method that prunes reasoning candidates early, balancing solution quality and computational cost during test-time inference.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, more efficient reasoning for large language models while maintaining accuracy.

items.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
items.summary: The paper studies how neural networks transition from using fixed random features to fully trainable representations, showing a phase change in approximation accuracy and training error.
items.whyItMatters: It reveals when and how neural nets shift from static to adaptive learning, guiding efficient model design.

items.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
items.summary: The article discusses monitoring AI decisions by auditing confidence scores to ensure reliable outcomes.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it improves trust and safety in AI systems.

items.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
items.summary: SpectralCanary introduces a simple low-frequency trace method to audit if a text-to-image model was fine-tuned on a specific image collection.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a lightweight, reliable way to detect hidden dataset usage in AI models.

items.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
items.summary: The article explores cost-aware abstention for LLM-based IT ticket classification, evaluating routing policies on calibration data and testing on a large ticket corpus.
items.whyItMatters: It shows how to reduce costly misrouting in IT support using AI, improving efficiency for tech operations.

items.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces METTA, a memory‑enhanced test‑time adaptation method for meta‑reinforcement learning that efficiently stores and retrieves long interaction histories.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, more scalable adaptation in RL agents, crucial for real‑world tasks with limited data and long horizons.

items.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
items.summary: EpiSEM-Bench tests how language‑model agents handle missing safety facts when using tools, assessing unsafe actions and evidence recovery.
items.whyItMatters: It helps developers ensure AI agents act safely even with incomplete tool outputs.

items.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
items.summary: The article discusses using low-bit n-gram embeddings to reduce memory usage in large language models.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it enables more efficient, scalable models with lower storage costs.

items.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
items.summary: The article identifies two numerical bugs in softmax and cross-entropy implementations that affect gradient behavior.
items.whyItMatters: Fixing these bugs ensures accurate training and better model convergence for AI practitioners.

items.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
items.summary: The paper investigates how chain-of-thought prompting can suffer from attention leakage, proposing context isolation to ensure reasoning steps causally influence the final answer.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it improves reliability of LLM explanations and reduces hallucinations.

items.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
items.summary: The article explores using an LLM-powered agent to debug a multilingual web corpus by generating test cases for each language, then having native speakers validate them.
items.whyItMatters: It shows how AI can uncover hidden language-specific errors in large datasets, improving NLP model reliability.

items.title: Bilingual Language Models Capture Cross-Linguistic Influence in Second-Language Reading
items.summary: While monolingual language model (LM) surprisal is widely established as a predictor of reading times, it cannot capture the non-native (L2) reading dynamics that are shaped by the reader's first language (L1). In this work, we investigate whether the cross-lingual transfer within bilingual models aligns with human L1-driven biases during L2 reading. We evaluate bilingual models on eye-tracking…

items.title: OP-Print: Tracing Membership Imprints in On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: On-policy distillation has been widely adopted for alleviating the distribution mismatch of off-policy distillation. Self-distillation further removes the need for an external teacher by using the student's own outputs, enhanced with extra context or demonstrations, as supervision. items.title: CRANE: Post-Hoc Counterfactual Retrieval for Multimodal Classifiers
items.summary: Counterfactual explanation methods have been introduced for unimodal settings, with dedicated frameworks for tabular, timeseries, text, and image data, yet no post-hoc method has been designed for classifiers that learn from multimodal inputs. items.summary: Control evaluations measure whether safeguards can prevent an AI model from causing undesired outcomes even when it is intentionally trying to do so.
